value.body: A nutritionist advises people and communities on what to eat for health. Employers include wellness and fitness companies, food and nutrition-product firms, corporate wellness programmes, NGOs and public-health nutrition projects. A typical day involves counselling clients, preparing diet plans and education material, and, in community work, running awareness sessions and collecting data.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Nutrition & Dietetics, Home Science (Food & Nutrition) or Food Science

items.label: Common settings
items.value: Wellness and fitness, food companies, NGOs, public-health programmes

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc in nutrition, dietetics or home science is the usual entry. Wellness firms, food companies and NGO projects hire freshers as nutrition counsellors or project staff; community nutrition posts under government schemes are often contractual and advertised by state or district bodies.

value.title: At a glance
items: The title is used loosely; clinical (hospital) work usually goes to dietitians with further training.
Next roles: senior nutritionist, programme coordinator, or a move to dietetics after an M.Sc and internship.
Freelance and online counselling are common but income varies.
